boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Marion-campus spaces for studying, creating, exercising, reflecting, meeting, and exploring between scheduled stops.

cards.title: Set Up for a Research Session
cards.subtitle: Study, meeting, and research space at the center of campus
cards.notes: Bring a research task or group agenda; the library provides workstations, wireless access, research help, and spaces designed for focused work.
cards.short_summary: A practical base for research help, computer access, and individual or collaborative study.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies Jackson Library on its Marion campus and says it provides spaces for studying, meeting, and research, plus workstations and research assistance.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service availability may vary by academic calendar; check university information before visiting.

cards.title: Keep Working After the Main Library Closes
cards.subtitle: A specifically documented round-the-clock study area
cards.notes: Use the lounge when coursework extends beyond regular library service hours; confirm entry rules and bring the campus credentials required for access.
cards.short_summary: The library’s designated option for study outside its standard staffed schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU’s library page explicitly lists a 24-hour study lounge among Jackson Library’s spaces for studying, meeting, and research.
cards.access_notes: The official page identifies this as a 24-hour study lounge; campus credential and holiday or break restrictions are not stated publicly.

cards.title: Record a Presentation Without a Full Production Setup
cards.subtitle: Reservable media studio on Jackson Library’s lower level
cards.notes: Reserve the studio for a video essay, presentation rehearsal, interview, or podcast; bring a thumb drive and do not book it for ordinary group study.
cards.short_summary: A student-accessible recording room built to simplify polished video and audio projects.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU says the lower-level Jackson Library studio is available by reservation to all IWU students, faculty, and staff for production uses including presentations and podcasts.
cards.access_notes: Reservation and IWU affiliation are required; the university states that the studio is for production rather than individual or group study.

cards.entity_name: Society of World Changers Hall of Honor
cards.title: Read the Stories Behind the Library Rotunda
cards.subtitle: Permanent bronze-bust display inside Jackson Library
cards.notes: Walk the rotunda slowly and use the displayed inductees as prompts for conversation, reflection, or follow-up research in the library.
cards.short_summary: A permanent campus collection that turns the library rotunda into a biographical gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU states that a life-size bronze bust of each Society of World Changers inductee is permanently displayed in the Hall of Honor in Jackson Library’s rotunda.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Jackson Library; visit during building access hours and follow current university visitor policies.

cards.title: Handle Several Campus Tasks in One Stop
cards.subtitle: Student-life hub with services, gathering areas, and dining
cards.notes: Use the building as a between-class waypoint for student services, the post office, bookstore, health center, academic support, or a planned meetup.
cards.short_summary: A shared campus hub where everyday errands and informal connection overlap.
cards.evidence_claim: The IWU catalog calls Barnes Student Center the Marion campus’s central hub and lists student services, gathering amenities, dining, a theater, post office, health center, and academic support.
cards.access_notes: Individual offices, venues, and dining operations maintain their own schedules and access requirements.

cards.title: Turn a Difficult Assignment Into a Work Plan
cards.subtitle: Academic-support space in Barnes Student Center
cards.notes: Arrive with a specific course question and ask about peer tutoring, academic coaching, structured study, writing help, or research support.
cards.short_summary: A collaborative academic-support setting for building skills and getting targeted help.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes The Learning Center as a central hub offering peer tutoring, academic coaching, structured study opportunities, and additional writing, research, and subject support.
cards.access_notes: The Center for Academic Thriving is listed in Barnes Student Center, Suite 260; confirm appointments and current service hours directly.

cards.title: Switch Between Solo Work and Peer Connection
cards.subtitle: Study-and-connect space within the Center for Academic Thriving
cards.notes: Choose this lounge when you want room to work independently but still stay near peers and academic-support staff in Barnes Student Center.
cards.short_summary: A flexible lounge intended for both independent study and working alongside others.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes The Thriving Lounge as a welcoming space where students can study, connect, and work either independently or alongside peers.
cards.access_notes: Located with the Center for Academic Thriving in Barnes Student Center, Suite 260; current open hours are not published on the cited page.

cards.title: Build Movement Into the Academic Day
cards.subtitle: Campus facility for recreation, training, and fitness
cards.notes: Check the activity areas and current schedule before going; student access covers recreational and training equipment, with some area-specific closures.
cards.short_summary: The Marion campus’s primary shared facility for exercise, recreation, and health education.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU identifies the Recreation and Wellness Center as its primary campus site for health education and fitness and says its recreational and training equipment is accessible to IWU students.
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours are Monday–Friday 6:00 a.m.–10:30 p.m., Saturday 8:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m., and Sunday 5:00–10:00 p.m.; area closures apply.

cards.title: Take a Quiet Pause Between Commitments
cards.subtitle: Campus sanctuary for prayer, reflection, and meditation
cards.notes: Step inside for a brief quiet reset, personal prayer, journaling, or reflection; respect the contemplative purpose and any posted use guidance.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated small-scale retreat from the pace of classes and campus activities.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU describes Williams Prayer Chapel as a sanctuary intended for personal prayer, reflection, and meditation on the Marion campus.
cards.access_notes: The cited university page does not publish current opening hours; observe posted access rules and scheduled uses.

cards.title: Use a Changing Exhibition as a Creative Reset
cards.subtitle: Gallery spaces located off Beard Art Center’s main lobby
cards.notes: Check for a current exhibition or artist visit, then bring a classmate to compare observations and discuss how the work was presented.
cards.short_summary: Rotating exhibitions create a recurring reason to step into Beard Art Center beyond class time.
cards.evidence_claim: IWU says Beard Art Center’s galleries are off the main lobby and host shifting exhibitions, visiting artists, lectures, and openings where students can meet professionals.
cards.access_notes: Exhibition and event schedules vary; verify current gallery access and any event-specific requirements before visiting.
